Name: Energy and Particle Technology Lab at Carleton Univeristy

The Energy and Particle Technology Laboratory at Carleton University is dedicated to developing technologies to decarbonize energy conversion and storage.  Our research is focused on micro and nanoparticle engineering with applications in process design and optimisation for energy conversion and storage, advanced material synthesis, novel hydrogen generation or carbon dioxide conversion processes, emission sensing and dispersion, and quantification of their impact on the environment.

We develop process design tools for scalable synthesis of nanoparticles with tailored functional properties and study how particle characteristics including their size distribution, morphology, and chemical composition are linked to their properties of interest such as optical, sensing, and energy storage characteristics.

We also develop novel processes and disruptive technologies for hydrogen generation and conversion of greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane into valuable products.

The patented device is certified as safe and non-toxic by the NSF, a non-profit organization dedicated to public safety and protection, and is authorized for sale by the Food and Drug Administration, or FDA.

The success of the Fryfresh device is attributed to a photo-catalytic nanotechnology that it utilizes to diminish oil breakdown at a molecular level, caused by oxidization, thereby prolonging its lifespan by as much as 150 percent. This allows establishment owners to reap substantial savings on both their cooking oil and oil disposal costs.

Furthermore, the reduction in oil breakdown allows for better heat transfer from oil to food, which ultimately provides for faster cooked foods and the shortening of cooking times by up to 25 percent. This subsequently cuts down on energy consumption by as much as 30 percent. A reduction in oil breakdown also enhances food flavor and lessens oil absorption by food items resulting in healthier eating.

The Fryfresh device is a recipient of the 2008 Kitchen InnovationsTM (KI) Award, bestowed by the National Restaurant Association, for addressing the growing needs of food service operators and improving productivity and food safety.

The average civilian requires approximately 20 disposable masks per month while the average front line medical worker consumes 5 to 7, N95 high-grade masks per day costing governments approximately $6,000USD per year in disposable waste per worker. The Nanoventi equivalent will cost less then 1/40th of that across 2 yrs and virtually eliminate environmental waste.

The primary shell of the respirator is made from a soft polymer which can be color tuned or left without pigment to produce crystal clear transparency. The mask contains a filtration platform of self-cleaning nanotubes and can be 100% sterilized using a conventional dishwasher or cold washed using CS20 cold sterilizing without degrading the structures or properties of the respirator.

The soft feel and effective nanoventing of the mask, as well as anti-fogging, make it an ideal choice for either medical or civilan applications

At the heart of our portfolio is the LVEM 5, the world’s first and only benchtop transmission electron microscope. Designed for powerful imaging in a remarkably small footprint, the LVEM 5 brings electron microscopy into laboratories that might otherwise lack the space, infrastructure, or budget for a conventional high-voltage instrument. Operating at low voltages, it enables fast, routine nanomaterials characterization and versatile imaging across TEM, SEM, STEM, and ED modes.

Building on this success, the LVEM 25E delivers the next generation of low voltage TEM. Combining the high resolution of field emission technology with the advantages of low voltage imaging, it produces nanometer-scale detail while preserving contrast in delicate or unstained samples. With optional EDS for chemical analysis, the LVEM 25E offers advanced performance while remaining easy to install, operate, and maintain. Applications range from clinical pathology and pharmaceutical R&D to advanced materials characterization.

What sets Delong apart is our philosophy: high-quality imaging should be within reach of every laboratory. Our microscopes require minimal infrastructure and are practical for a wide variety of environments. By lowering barriers to access, we empower researchers, educators, and innovators to explore the nanoscale with confidence.

Delong Instruments is your way to electron microscopy.

Therapeutic heat (41-48°C) stimulates the immune system, shrinks tumors, inactivates cancer stem cells, and increases tumor perfusion – thus enabling drugs to reach all tumor compartments more effectively. The size, shape, and surface chemistry of the gold nanorods target the leaky vasculature of solid tumors, and the selective thermal sensitivity of tumor tissue enables the therapy to deliver clean margins. Targeted Hyperthermia Therapy promises to be safe, effective, minimally invasive, competitive in cost, and a valuable adjunct to drug therapy and other cancer treatments.  

Sona has developed multiple proprietary methods for the manufacture of gold nanoparticles which it uses for the development of both cancer therapies and diagnostic testing platforms. Sona Nanotech’s gold nanorod particles are cetyltrimethylammonium (“CTAB”) free, eliminating the toxicity risks associated with the use of other gold nanorod technologies in medical applications with an assessment by the Nanotechnology Characterisation Laboratory that detected neither endotoxins nor microbial contamination. It is expected that Sona’s gold nanotechnologies may be adapted for use in applications, as a safe and effective delivery system for multiple medical treatments, subject to the approval of various regulatory boards, including Health Canada and the FDA.

Description:

Our set of DFT-based software is being used around the world by Universities, Government labs and private R&D companies to reduce development costs and time-to-market.

We have also developed an innovative and unique spin-qubit modeling tool to simulate the envelope functions of elementary particles in semiconductors, in the design of your choice and study its quantum properties to design the components of future quantum computers. QTCAD calculates the envelope functions and energy levels of electrons or holes confined in nanostructures within k.p theory by using non-linear Poisson, Schrödinger, and many-body solvers. 
The next evolution of QTCAD will consist in implementing more exclusive features for spin-qubit modeling with in particular Tight-Binding (TB) simulation capabilities and also a new software module to simulate superconducting-qubit based device parameters with finite element modeling and Josephson junctions material properties with atomistic methods which is a multiscale approach, truly unique on the market by bridging our atomistic and quantum design code ecosystems.

It is commercially available for academic and corporate users and a classroom version for graduate students is available, it is QTCAD EDU available for free-trial testing and through semester/year-long licenses.

Our customers' fields of research are semiconductors, nanomaterials and devices, battery technologies, solar cells, metals, topological materials, quantum computing technologies and telecommunication among plenty of other innovative materials science and applicative domains.

https://docs.nanoacademic.com/

Name: Applied Nanotools Inc.
Description:
Welcome to Applied Nanotools Inc. (ANT), a pioneering nanofabrication company specializing in integrated photonics, EUV and X-ray optics. Established in 2002, our mission is to expand the horizons of photonics and X-ray technologies, empowering our clients to achieve breakthroughs in imaging, sensing, communication, computing, and beyond. Leveraging 100 keV electron beam lithography technology, our processes can produce photonic circuits (down to 60 nm feature size for Si) and X-ray optics (down to 12 nm) at the nanoscale. Our team of specialists are committed to delivering tailored solutions that align with the unique requirements of each project, ensuring the utmost quality and performance.

ANT’s unwavering commitment to nanofabrication has given rise to the NanoSOI rapid-prototyping silicon photonics foundry service. With over 400 peer-reviewed publications utilizing the platform, it has become a core technology for a wide-range of universities and companies worldwide. Our NanoSOI Design Center showcases a range of services (MPW & custom/dedicated runs) including design, fabrication, and characterization that revolutionize the way optical systems are fabricated, offering unparalleled performance, rapid turn-around time and cost-effectiveness to our researchers and customers. 

Whether you're looking to develop advanced photonics for telecommunications, high-resolution X-ray optics for imaging, or cutting-edge solutions for quantum technologies, we have the expertise and capabilities to turn your vision into reality. 

Join us in shaping the future of integrated photonics, x-ray optics, EUV optics, membrane optics, and metalenses as we continue to expand. Together, we can unlock new possibilities and drive innovation to new heights.
For more details, please visit our website: www.appliednt.com

Our instruments provide customers with a bench-top system for rapid, inexpensive, and automated fabrication and experimentation with precisely sized solid-state nanopores for use in a variety of life and health sciences research. Name: Plasmionique Inc.
Description:
At Plasmionique Inc., we bring over 26 years of expertise in plasma technology, combining scientific innovation with engineering excellence to develop custom-built systems for Surface Engineering, Advanced Materials Synthesis, Thin-Film Coatings, and Nanotechnology.

Our adaptable and highly skilled team thrives on innovation, designing cutting-edge, tailored solutions to meet the unique needs of researchers and industries worldwide. Description: Bio Graphene Solutions (BGS) is a manufacturer and supplier of graphene from non-graphite based, organic renewable resources. Name: Functional Coating and Surface Engineering Laboratory (FCSEL)
Description:
The FCSEL (Functional Coating and Surface Engineering Laboratory) is an academic research laboratory that focuses on the development of innovative vacuum- and plasma-based processes and materials for coatings and thin film systems with tailored functional and multifunctional characteristics. With a long history of industrial partnerships spanning more than three decades, the FCSEL has developed a unique global (or holistic) approach to technological challenges and surface engineering solutions based on a simultaneous action, within the same laboratory, of several key elements including an in-depth understanding of the application problem and the availability of the appropriate metrology tools (testing methods) to quantitatively assess the coating system’s main functional characteristics as well as stability and durability in a working environment. Only then can an appropriate solution be sought in terms of nanostructured coating materials and their integration into specific coating architectures, while applying suitable fabrication processes, modeling approaches, and life cycle analysis.

Targeted functional coating characteristics include optical, optoelectronic, micro- and nano-mechanical, tribological, and protective properties for their application in various areas, such as optics, photonics, optoelectronics, aerospace and space exploration, biomedicine, automotive industry, security, energy saving, manufacturing and many others.

This access to the most advanced fabrication and characterization equipment under the same roof renders the FCSEL an exclusive highly dynamic and stimulating environment for training the next generation of engineers and scientists who will tackle the world’s present and future challenges. It also offers a stimulating environment for university-industry collaborations and partnerships, as well as punctual services.

Name: Waterloo Nanotechnology Conference
Description:
WNC is a student-organized conference that provides an opportunity for students, employers, and entrepreneurs to learn from one another, strengthening our mutual understanding about how nanotechnology is taught and how it is used in industry, in innovative research, and how it is powering new ventures.
We will educate and inspire our participants with exciting speakers, an informative industry panel discussion, and other interactive activities.

After having started in 2015 with an event organized by 6 Nanotechnology Engineering students, the annual conference has attracted everyone – ranging from high-school students to seasoned senior undergraduates to graduate students –  who seeks an exclusive opportunity to learn about different career paths and the opportunities and resources available to them. The conference now takes place annually in November, attracting over 200 students from Waterloo and elsewhere, as well as renown speakers who use nanotechnology to make an impact in their work.

The conference is supported by the University of Waterloo Office of Research, Faculties of Science and Engineering, Waterloo Institute for Nanotechnology, Nanotechnology Engineering Program, and Materials and Nanosciences Program at UW.

Name: Anasens
Description: Anasens is a highly disruptive start-up (deep tech) developing an innovative quantitative and connected molecular detection platform for blood or saliva analysis, at home or at a point of service, in less than 5 minutes. Name: De France Lab
Description:
Driving cellulose and protein research toward a sustainable future | At Queen's University

Our research program explores the design of sustainable bio-based materials and their application in fields spanning the biomedical, coatings & packaging, and environmental sectors. Specifically, we focus on cellulose- and protein-based nanomaterial ‘building blocks’ such as cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs), cellulose nanofibers (CNFs), and protein nanofibers to make structures including hydrogels, aerogels, emulsions, and films. We aim to understand and leverage structure-function relationships to precisely tailor material performance for targeted applications. The work in our lab is interdisciplinary, spanning materials chemistry, engineering, and biotechnology, with the end goal of replacing petroleum-based products with high-performance renewable materials for a greener future.

Description: Direct-C leverages a proprietary, nano-composite polymer platform technology that can be used for two main applications, sensing a variety of chemical species or measuring strain. Name: nFluids Inc.
Description:
Based in Alberta, Canada, nFluids was incorporated in 2012 to solve oil and gas drilling fluid challenges using leading edge nanotechnology.

Today, nFluids Inc. is an innovative nanotechnology company that manufactures cost-effective nanoparticle additives.  The team’s focus forms the basis of four filed patent applications that defines nFluids’ technology platform.  Using similar processes and materials, nFluids plans to use the technology to solve related challenges in other industries.

By using controlled chemical reactions we are able to control the size, shape, functionality, and final concentration of the nanoparticles. This mechanism allows us to offer unique solutions to our clients for high-volume bulk processes or bespoke applications.

nForcerTM, the first commercial product, is a high-performing, multi-functional drilling fluid additive compatible with all mud types. nForcerTM is a true platform technology in that this product can be used in applications beyond oil and gas.

Name: Scope Photonics Inc
Description:
Typical glass and plastic lenses use digital cropping or physical movement to zoom - a ridiculous limitation for the twenty first century. We’re building lenses capable of lossless zoom without any movement, using our novel liquid crystal technology. They can instantly adjust their optical behaviour to take the perfect photo, no matter the situation. 

This presents enormous benefits for smartphone photography, which normally relies on digital cropping or multiple apertures to zoom and take great photos. Our lenses can quickly adjust their zoom without pixelation, correct for optical aberrations, and adapt for any condition to take the best photo possible. No need for multiple apertures - one of our lens systems built into a smartphone can do it all.

It's not just smartphones that need better lenses. Numerous industries, from virtual reality to LiDAR sensing to microscopy, all suffer from fixed lens limitations. Our technology is transferable across applications; a paradigm shift for optics.

Name: CERC interactions lumière-matière/light-matter interactions
Description:
La vision haut niveau de la Chaire d'excellence en recherche du Canada (CERC) sur les interactions lumière-matière est d'apporter de nouvelles connaissances sur les propriétés des systèmes microscopiques constitués de nombreuses particules en interaction à l'état solide, ce qui permettra de découvrir et de mettre en œuvre de nouveaux matériaux pour la photonique et les technologies quantiques. 
***
The high-level vision of the Canada Excellence Research Chair (CERC) in Light-Matter Interactions is to deliver new knowledge of the properties of microscopic systems made of many interacting particles in the solid state, which will empower the discovery and implementation of new materials for photonics and quantum technologies.

Name: ArcticEdge Technologies
Description:
PFAS bans are creating a major gap in the textile industry: the world still needs materials that are breathable, waterproof, durable, and safe.

ArcticEdge Technologies is building a new class of PFAS-free breathable waterproof fabric for high-performance applications, from rainwear and PPE to firefighting gear. Unlike traditional moisture barriers that rely on multiple laminated layers, our material is designed as a single functional fabric that can deliver protection, comfort, and manufacturability in one layer.

We’re starting with firefighting because the problem is urgent, the standards are demanding, and the need for safer protective gear is impossible to ignore. But the vision is bigger: a PFAS-free future for breathable waterproof textiles.

Name: Resolve Nanotherapeutics Corp.
Description: Resolve Nanotherapeutics (RNTx) is developing completely novel drugs for severe infections such as pneumonia, abdominal infections and others. These types of infections kill millions of people every year and our current frontline treatments – antibiotics – are rapidly losing their effectiveness due to the rise in antibiotic resistance. RNTx is taking a host-directed approach to address this problem and using cutting-edge lipid nanoparticle (LNP) RNA technology to activate the body’s natural toxin clearance systems, ultimately overcoming the devastating clinical complications and vital organ dysfunction that accompany these types of severe infections. RNTx is the product of a collaboration between the UBC labs of Dr. Pieter Cullis (LNP expert) and Dr. James Russell (critical care physician and researcher) developing de-risked technology packages in pre-clinical models of severe infection. Studies to date have demonstrated remarkable efficacy in an in vivo model of pneumonia caused by antibiotic resistant bacteria. The key strengths of the technology are: (1) that the approach is organism and antibiotic resistance agnostic, (2) it does not create a selective pressure for new resistance development, ensuring a sustained market once approved and, (3) it uses clinically validated components (LNPs and RNA) that can readily be scaled for manufacturing and widespread distribution.

Name: Microbonds Inc.
Description: Incorporated in 1996, Microbonds Inc. is a pioneer in advanced material science and nanotechnology coatings, initially for the semiconductor packaging and microchip industries. Name: WeckLab
Description: We are a group of researchers whose interests lie at the intersection of photonics, materials science, chemistry, and surface engineering. We use ultrafast lasers to texture the surface of materials to control properties such as colours, wettability, chemical reactions, and biocompatibility. We also use these lasers for high speed micro-machining, fundamental laser-matter interaction studies, and to induce artificial defects (crack and voids) to investigate fracture mechanisms

Name: Carbosphere Inc
Description:
Carbosphere as developed a sustainable and cost-efficient decarbonisation solution for industrial and municipal waste which enables us to optimize the recycling process of all hydrocarbons base materials. Deployed on a large scale, this technology would make a significant contribution towards the 2050 net zero target.

While 95% of the global hydrogen is gray, it releases nine to 12 tonnes of CO2 for every tonne of hydrogen produced. At Carbosphere, we produce low-emission hydrogen and a solid carbon co-products rather than releasing CO2, we strive to solve the high-emission challenges of gray hydrogen and the economic and intrant challenges of green hydrogen.

We support industries in their decarbonisation journey to reduce pollution, reach sustainable development and become leaders in the circular economy, all while providing opportunities to reach both the solid nanostructure carbon and the hydrogen market.

Name: Nano Imaging and Spectroscopy Laboratory
Description:
The Nano-Imaging and Spectroscopy Laboratory (NISL) at Ontario Tech University is a cutting-edge interdisciplinary research group focused on advancing fundamental and applied science at the nanoscale. Led by Dr. Nisha Agarwal, NISL integrates expertise from materials chemistry, physics, biophysics, and spectroscopy to explore the interactions of light and matter in complex systems.

Our research spans a broad spectrum—from plasmonic nanostructures and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) to radiation-sensitive biosensors, laser-deposited materials, and vibrational spectroscopy for medical diagnostics. We are committed to innovation at the intersection of nanotechnology, photonics, and life sciences.

At NISL, we combine state-of-the-art instrumentation with hands-on training for undergraduate and graduate students, fostering the next generation of interdisciplinary researchers. We welcome collaborations and new team members passionate about solving real-world challenges using nanoscience.

 Key Areas:
• Nano- and bio-materials characterization
• Surface-enhanced spectroscopy (SERS, SEF)
• Radiation effects on biomolecules
• Optical and energy sensor development
• Medical and environmental diagnostics
